instruction: Among the PLOS ONE correction records indexed as Published Erratum with publication dates in June 2015, which announce that an article was republished to correct its title? Catalogue each affected research article with its DOI, the republication date stated by the notice, the complete title on the originally published uncorrected article, and the complete title on the republished corrected article. The June range applies to publication of the correction notice, not initial publication or republication of the research article. Include only notices announcing republication for an article-title correction; ordinary title corrections that do not announce republication, and republications for other stated reasons, do not qualify. Use source records available by 9 September 2026. Preserve the original title’s spelling even when it is erroneous; current corrected metadata is not a substitute for the originally published title. Establish the complete notice corpus, distinguish a title correction from an announced republication, and follow each qualifying notice to the versions it identifies. Separate notice and republication dates. Check the uncorrected and corrected title evidence for the same research-article DOI; bibliographic repositories can retain different title states. Public APIs, bulk downloads and equivalent independently verifiable source paths are allowed.
output_format: Return only a pipe-separated table with header article_doi|republication_date|original_title|corrected_title. Use bare DOI values and YYYY-MM-DD dates. Give the complete titles as plain text, without quotation marks, italics, line breaks, or an added final period; capitalization differences are accepted. Preserve word spelling and punctuation, using ordinary hyphens for hyphens. Sort by article_doi.
